questions.question_text: The term "marginal cost" refers to

options.C: Cost of producing one additional unit

questions.explanation: Marginal cost is the incremental cost incurred to produce or distribute one additional unit of a product. In pure software products, marginal cost is near zero ($MC \approx 0$).

questions.question_text: What is a Product Family?

options.A: A collection of unrelated products sold by a company
options.B: A set of products sharing a strong brand identity and marketed together
options.C: A set of products built on a common codebase only
options.D: A group of products sold in one country

questions.explanation: A Product Family is a collection of diverse, functional products unified under a single, strong brand name for marketing, trust-building, and cross-selling benefits.

questions.question_text: The ultimate objective of Software Product Management is to

options.B: Generate the greatest possible business value

questions.explanation: The ultimate goal of SPM is to maximize sustainable business value by continuously solving real customer problems effectively rather than simply shipping features.

questions.question_text: The primary goal of the DFV framework is to

options.D: Balance customer needs, technical capability, and business success

questions.explanation: The DFV Framework ensures product viability by balancing Desirability (customer needs), Feasibility (engineering capability), and Viability (business sustainability).

questions.question_text: The caterpillar-versus-butterfly analogy is used to illustrate that

options.C: Startups are fundamentally different from established companies

questions.explanation: Coined by Steve Blank, this analogy emphasizes that a startup is not merely a smaller version of a mature company; it operates under extreme uncertainty searching for a repeatable business model.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best illustrates the Social Impact level?

options.C: Enabling financial inclusion at scale through UPI

questions.explanation: The pinnacle of Bain's Value Pyramid is Social Impact, which delivers self-transcendence and societal transformation, such as UPI driving universal financial inclusion across a nation.

questions.question_text: What problem does the Value Proposition Canvas primarily address?

options.C: Value Gap between product and customer needs

questions.explanation: The Value Proposition Canvas systematically maps the Customer Profile to the Value Map to bridge and eliminate the gap between customer needs and product offerings.

questions.question_text: Which phrase best summarizes the TAM-SAM-SOM strategy?
questions.explanation: "Think big, start small" reflects envisioning a large Total Addressable Market (TAM) while executing tightly by starting with Early Evangelists within the Serviceable Obtainable Market (SOM).

questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of the Learning Loop?
questions.explanation: The Build-Measure-Learn loop accelerates validated learning using user data to refine product hypotheses and minimize market risk.

questions.question_text: What is the "Chasm" in Moore's model?

options.A: Gap between early adopters and early majority
options.B: Gap between innovators and early adopters
options.C: Gap between early majority and late majority
options.D: Gap between late majority and laggards

questions.explanation: In Geoffrey Moore's Technology Adoption Life Cycle, the Chasm represents the critical adoption gap separating visionary Early Adopters from pragmatic Early Majority buyers.

questions.question_text: Which statement best distinguishes Product Definition from Positioning?

options.A: Product Definition explains customer value; Positioning explains technical architecture.
options.B: Product Definition describes what the product does; Positioning explains why customers should choose it.
options.C: Both serve exactly the same purpose.

questions.explanation: Product Definition is an internal operational statement of functional capabilities, whereas Product Positioning is an external statement establishing value and differentiation against alternatives.

questions.question_text: A consumer fitness app offers a free version, encourages social sharing, and relies on app store downloads. This GTM approach is primarily:
questions.explanation: A GTM strategy leveraging self-service onboarding, freemium access, viral sharing mechanics, and digital app store distribution is a classic Product-Led B2C model.

questions.question_text: Which growth strategy generally has the lowest Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC)?
questions.explanation: Product-Led Growth relies on the product experience itself to drive self-service acquisition and organic virality, significantly lowering human sales and marketing CAC.

questions.question_text: A software company earns more revenue from consulting projects than from software licenses, causing the product roadmap to slow down. Which startup mistake best describes this situation?
questions.explanation: Becoming reliant on custom service projects distracts engineering teams from building scalable core software products, effectively turning the product company into an IT consulting agency.

questions.question_text: A CRM vendor allows customers to install marketplace apps without changing the core product. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: Composition refers to extending product capabilities via modular external applications or plugins without altering the core codebase.

questions.question_text: Which factor most strongly determines customers' willingness to pay?
questions.explanation: In value-based pricing, price is dictated by the net perceived economic benefit and outcome derived by the customer rather than internal development costs or feature volume.

questions.question_text: A startup has a large consumer user base but very low willingness to pay. Which revenue model is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: An ad-supported revenue model monetizes high user attention and traffic from non-paying users by selling ad inventory to third-party advertisers.

questions.question_text: Which product decision is most likely to shorten the CAC payback period?

options.A: Improving customer activation and early value realisation

questions.explanation: Streamlining onboarding to help users realize value quickly accelerates initial revenue capture and subscription retention, directly shortening the CAC payback window.

questions.question_text: Why is forecasting particularly difficult for software startups?

options.B: Startups usually operate with limited historical data and uncertain markets.

questions.explanation: Startups operate under conditions of extreme market uncertainty lacking historical telemetry data, making deterministic financial projections challenging.

questions.question_text: As startups mature, investor evaluation shifts primarily from

options.B: Vision and founder quality to predictable growth and scalable economics

questions.explanation: In early stages investors back founder quality and vision, but as a startup matures, focus shifts strictly to unit economics, CAC payback, and predictable growth metrics.

questions.question_text: A software company intentionally provides APIs, SDKs, and revenue-sharing programs to encourage third-party innovation. Which ecosystem strategy is it following?
questions.explanation: Keystone players foster open, supportive partner networks by sharing platform value via APIs, SDKs, and joint monetization opportunities.

questions.question_text: Which activity is most closely associated with a Go-to-Market (GTM) strategy?
questions.explanation: Go-to-Market (GTM) strategy focuses on launch execution, positioning, marketing channels, and commercial alignment to drive market adoption.

questions.question_text: A company receives excellent CSAT scores but low NPS scores. What is the most likely interpretation?

options.A: Customers are satisfied but unwilling to recommend the product.

questions.explanation: CSAT measures short-term satisfaction with specific support/feature interactions, while NPS measures long-term brand advocacy and willingness to recommend.

questions.question_text: A startup has completed product development but customers are largely unaware that the problem exists. According to the Product Launch Framework, the company should first:
questions.explanation: In the Unawareness stage of the buyer's journey, the primary objective is publishing thought-leadership and educational content to raise problem awareness.

questions.question_text: Which Product Management responsibility is most critical during the Purchase stage?
questions.explanation: During the purchase/onboarding phase, PMs must ensure frictionless user account setup and minimize Time-to-First-Value (TTFV) to prevent drop-offs.
